result.note: Tests the sequence of cheetah translocations from three African source countries under India's reintroduction project.

questions.prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to cheetahs brought to India under the project to reintroduce the species:
questions.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain: All three pairs are correct. Namibia sent eight cheetahs in September 2022, South Africa sent 12 in February 2023 and Botswana sent nine in February 2026, to restore a species that went extinct in India in 1952. In October 2026, a litter of five at Kuno National Park took India's cheetah count to 60, and the cubs' Botswanan father starts a new genetic line.
questions.source: Botswana's nine cheetahs arrived in February, following eight from Namibia in September 2022 and 12 from South Africa in February 2023, under a project to restore a species that went extinct in India in 1952.
